fields.subnational_unit: rural South Africa (no single site; literature-based)
fields.population: rural women in South Africa as described in the secondary literature (water collection, subsistence farming, household management)
fields.sample_size: no primary sample: textual analysis of existing literature (about 100 cited sources) through a feminist political ecology lens; no search strategy or selection criteria stated
fields.effect_measure: conceptual narrative analysis of secondary literature (feminist political ecology); no quantitative measure
fields.effect_estimate: Women carry water collection (cited: 56% of adult women, 31% of girls and 3% of boys in rural areas; loads averaging 19.5 kg over about 337 m with 69% reporting back pain, from cited sources), face intensified labour, reduced income opportunities and health risks; formal and informal water institutions (WUAs, irrigation committees, traditional authorities, water services authorities) exclude women from decision-making despite constitutional right-to-water and Free Basic Water policy (about 6 kl per household per month). Recommends gender-sensitive infrastructure and institutional reform for women's inclusion in water governance. No original data.
fields.model_type: secondary-data conceptual analysis; textual analysis of literature
fields.study_design: non-systematic secondary literature review / conceptual analysis (no primary empirical data)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a non-systematic, desk-based conceptual analysis of secondary literature on gender and water scarcity in rural South Africa (feminist political ecology), read in full text 2026-10-04. No primary data, no search or selection method, no effect estimate; it cites but does not test legal and institutional arrangements. Inclusion criterion 3 (empirical evidence or a systematic synthesis) is doubtful.
